headline: All majors below the 200-day line with neutral momentum, but whales are pulling coins off exchange while retail ETF flows turned red today.
paragraphs: The regime is unambiguous: Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, XRP, BNB, Doge, and Cardano are all trading below their 200-day simple moving averages, and none have achieved a golden cross. There is no asset in this cohort above trend. Bitcoin sits 49.1 percent below its 12-month high of $124,739, Ethereum 61.4 percent below $4,817, and the long-tail altcoins are bleaker still, Cardano trades 80.9 percent down from $0.9631. This is a downtrend regime by definition. The bounce off the lows (Bitcoin up 1.13 percent over seven days, Ethereum up 0.76, ADA up 5.52) offers no technical vindication: all three majors have momentum readings near neutral. Bitcoin's RSI sits at 46, Ethereum at 47.9, and XRP, the weakest of the group, prints 33.3, well into oversold territory but with MACD still below its signal line. Only Solana, BNB, and Doge show MACD above signal, a mild bullish divergence from price, but each remains below its 200-day line. The message from momentum and trend is consistent: there is no acceleration in either direction, and the underlying structure remains bearish.

Positioning in perpetual futures reveals a market heavy on the long side with funding rates that range from neutral to expensive. Bitcoin's 8-hour funding sits at 0.01 percent, equivalent to 11.0 percent annualized, a rate paid by longs to shorts, modest but non-trivial. Ethereum's funding is even lower at 0.0065 percent (7.1 annualized), suggesting less urgency to hold longs, yet the long-to-short ratio stands at 1.78 on OKX, meaning 78 percent more leverage deployed long than short. Solana shows the most imbalance: funding is nearly flat at -0.0001 percent (slightly shorts pay), yet the long-short ratio hits 2.0, a 100 percent skew toward longs. Liquidations in the last 24 hours reveal a skew toward long exits: Bitcoin liquidated 11.1 million in longs versus 459 thousand in shorts, a roughly 24-to-1 ratio. Ethereum saw 8.3 million in long liquidations against 1.2 million in shorts. This pattern, expensive long funding combined with lopsided long-side liquidations, suggests the crowd is neither calmly holding nor being forcibly shaken out; instead, the system is in a state of selective pruning of overleveraged longs. Open interest remains substantial (Bitcoin 2.04 billion, Ethereum 1.31 billion), so the boat is full enough to matter.

Spot flows from the traditional-finance side turned negative on the latest day: Bitcoin spot ETFs printed negative 144.6 million on 10 August, and Ethereum recorded negative 14.6 million the same date. Over the prior five sessions, the net was positive (Bitcoin plus 550.6 million, Ethereum plus 241 million), so this is a one-day reversal rather than a shift in the longer trend. Cumulative spot ETF inflows remain deeply positive (Bitcoin at 52.1 billion, Ethereum at 11.5 billion since inception), so the strategic bid from the traditional side persists, but momentum has stalled. Whale activity over the last 24 hours, by contrast, moved in the opposite direction: 121.5 million net moved off exchanges, driven chiefly by Bitcoin (65.3 million out) and Ethereum (56.2 million out). The largest single move was 128.9 million in BTC from Kraken, followed by 73.5 million from OKEx. Stablecoin-denominated buying power turned negative at negative 29.9 million, meaning more stablecoins moved onto exchanges than off, an unusual counterpoint to the BTC and ETH exodus. The weekly net flow over the most recent four weeks shows violent swings: minus 237.8 million, then plus 1.12 billion, plus 1.10 billion, then minus 394.8 million. This choppiness suggests uncertainty rather than conviction in either direction.

Fear and Greed sits at 29 (Fear), toward the low end of its 30-day range of 22 to 33, so the crowd's temperament matches the downtrend. Sentiment and tape are aligned here, which reduces the diagnostic power of the divergence test. Total market capitalization fell 0.53 percent in 24 hours to 2.27 trillion, and Bitcoin dominance stands firm at 56.4 percent, meaning the market cap loss was distributed, not concentrated in alts. Stablecoin float sits at 305.4 billion, down 1.38 percent on the month, modest dry powder, neither a flood nor a drought. Network vitals for Bitcoin show ordinary conditions: fastest fees at 4 satoshis per byte, difficulty down 2.0 percent with 1,628 blocks to retarget, suggesting the recent activity did not strain the chain.

The tape presents a market in retest mode: trends are down, momentum is neutral to slightly bullish on a handful of names, positioning is long-heavy but under selective stress, and flows are contradictory across time horizons and participant types. ETF buyers backed away on day one; whales pulled coins to cold storage; stablecoin pressure moved toward exchanges, not away. The one clear signal is the structural regime: nothing is above its 200-day line. A reader watching this would look for a reclaim of the 200-day by at least two of the three majors (Bitcoin, Ethereum, or Solana) or a reversal in whale flow direction persisting for a week or more as the condition that would change the picture.
